title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 334 (Transfers, etc., after commencement of winding up to be void)

content.overview: In a winding up by the Tribunal, any disposition of the property (including actionable claims) of the company and any transfer of shares in the company or alteration in the status of its members, made after the commencement of the winding up, shall, unless the Tribunal otherwise orders, be void.
content.glance: Post-commencement dispositions of property, share transfers and status alterations are void unless the Tribunal orders otherwise.
content.study: Section 334 protects the integrity of the estate after the commencement of a Tribunal winding up. Any disposition of company property (including actionable claims), any transfer of shares, or any alteration in the status of members made after commencement is void unless the Tribunal orders otherwise. The provision freezes the company’s property and membership position so that the liquidator can administer the estate without competing private dispositions.

sections.heading: Void post-commencement acts
sections.body: Disposition of property (including actionable claims), transfer of shares, or alteration in members’ status after commencement of Tribunal winding up is void unless Tribunal otherwise orders.

provisions.title: Transfers, etc., after commencement of winding up to be void

examples.title: Post-commencement sale
examples.body: After a winding-up order is made, a director causes the company to sell a valuable asset without Tribunal leave. The disposition is void under s. 334 unless the Tribunal subsequently validates it.

hypotheticals.question: Is a share transfer after commencement of Tribunal winding up valid?
hypotheticals.analysis: No, unless the Tribunal otherwise orders; s. 334 renders such transfers void.

rows.right: Within one year before petition or voluntary resolution

misconceptions.trap: The liquidator can freely dispose of assets without any Tribunal involvement after commencement.
misconceptions.correction: Private dispositions after commencement are void unless the Tribunal otherwise orders; the liquidator acts under the statutory scheme and Tribunal supervision.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 334 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm Tribunal winding up and the date of commencement. II. Identify the disposition, share transfer or status alteration. III. Conclude voidness unless Tribunal validation is obtained.

examTips: Emphasise ‘unless the Tribunal otherwise orders’ and the three categories of acts.
revisionPoints: Post-commencement dispositions void unless Tribunal orders otherwise
